items.answer: Capital: coffee machine and refit (non-current assets in the statement of financial position, depreciated). Revenue: wages and beans (expenses in the statement of profit or loss).
items.markingKey: Capital: coffee machine and refit (non-current assets in the statement of financial position, depreciated). Revenue: wages and beans (expenses in the statement of profit or loss).

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Businesses should cut capital expenditure during a recession."
items.answer: Cutting non-essential capital spending is prudent, but firms with strong finances may gain by investing counter-cyclically.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: preserves cash and reduces borrowing; demand is weak, so new capacity is not needed; reduces risk. Arguments against: asset prices and interest rates may be low; investment prepares for recovery; competitors may gain an advantage; delaying maintenance raises future costs. Supported judgement: Cutting non-essential capital spending is prudent, but firms with strong finances may gain by investing counter-cyclically.

items.markingKey: It has an opportunity cost: the money could have been paid to shareholders as dividends or invested elsewhere. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Read the extract.

Airlines have high fixed costs (aircraft leases, maintenance, staff), so they use dynamic pricing to fill seats; an empty seat earns nothing but costs almost the same.

With reference to the extract, analyse what the case of airline fixed costs shows about fixed and variable costs. [4]
items.answer: High fixed costs mean each extra passenger adds a lot to profit once variable costs are covered

items.stem: Fjord Outdoor needs equipment costing €80,000. Option A: a bank loan at 8% simple interest per year, repaid in full after 4 years. Option B: leasing the equipment for €2,310 a month for 4 years, after which it is returned. Calculate the total cost of each option and recommend one, giving one non-financial reason.
items.answer: A: €80,000 + interest €25,600 = €105,600 (and the firm owns the asset). B: €2,310 × 48 = €110,880 (no ownership). The loan is cheaper overall; non-financial: leasing includes maintenance/upgrades and preserves borrowing capacity, while the loan gives ownership and residual value.
items.markingKey: Interest = 80,000 × 8% × 4 = 25,600; loan total 105,600; lease total 2,310 × 48 = 110,880. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both totals. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [R1] justified recommendation.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of this view: "Reducing fixed costs is the best way for a business to increase profit."
items.answer: The best approach depends on the cost structure: high fixed-cost firms gain most from higher volume, while others may benefit from cost cuts.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: lowers break-even point; reduces risk in downturns; outsourcing turns fixed into variable costs. Arguments against: cutting fixed costs may reduce capacity and quality; raising revenue may be more effective; variable cost savings matter at high output. Supported judgement: The best approach depends on the cost structure: high fixed-cost firms gain most from higher volume, while others may benefit from cost cuts.

items.stem:
In 2020 many airlines cut revenue expenditure such as staff costs through furlough schemes while delaying capital expenditure on new aircraft.

Using the extract where relevant, analyse the advantages and disadvantages of acting on the view that businesses should cut capital expenditure during a recession. [8]
items.answer: Cutting non-essential capital spending is prudent, but firms with strong finances may gain by investing counter-cyclically.
items.markingKey: Advantages: preserves cash and reduces borrowing; demand is weak, so new capacity is not needed; reduces risk. Disadvantages: asset prices and interest rates may be low; investment prepares for recovery; competitors may gain an advantage; delaying maintenance raises future costs. 7-8: balanced analysis applied to the case; 5-6: analysis of both sides, partly applied; 3-4: one-sided or generic; 1-2: descriptive.

items.stem:
Pebble raised over $10 m from about 69,000 backers on Kickstarter in 2012, then over $20 m in 2015, but was sold to Fitbit in 2016 after financial difficulties.

Using the extract where relevant, analyse the advantages and disadvantages of acting on the view that share capital is the best source of finance for a growing company. [8]
items.answer: Share capital suits large, risky long-term investments, but debt or retained profit may be cheaper and preserve control for stable businesses.
items.markingKey: Advantages: no repayment or interest; large amounts available; lower gearing. Disadvantages: dilution of control; dividend expectations; cost and time of issue; risk of takeover. 7-8: balanced analysis applied to the case; 5-6: analysis of both sides, partly applied; 3-4: one-sided or generic; 1-2: descriptive.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "overdraft"?
options: Assets held by a business for more than twelve months, such as property, plant and equipment
An arrangement in which suppliers allow a business to pay for goods some time after delivery, usually 30-90 days
A facility that allows a business to withdraw more money than it has in its bank account, up to an agreed limit, for short-term needs
Costs that change directly with the level of output, such as raw materials and packaging
items.answer: A facility that allows a business to withdraw more money than it has in its bank account, up to an agreed limit, for short-term needs
items.markingKey: C. "overdraft" is a facility that allows a business to withdraw more money than it has in its bank account, up to an agreed limit, for short-term needs.

items.answer: Costs that do not change with the level of output in the short run, such as rent, insurance and salaries

items.stem:
Read the extract.

Saudi Aramco raised about $25.6 bn in its December 2019 IPO, then the largest ever.

Explain why retained profit is often the cheapest source of finance. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: There are no interest payments, fees or loss of control; however, it has an opportunity cost because shareholders give up dividends.
items.markingKey: There are no interest payments, fees or loss of control; however, it has an opportunity cost because shareholders give up dividends. items.stem:
Read the extract.

Netflix introduced a cheaper ad-supported plan in 2022 and began charging for password sharing in 2023, adding advertising revenue to subscriptions.

Explain why businesses try to develop several revenue streams. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: Several sources of income spread risk, increase total revenue and use existing assets and customers more fully (e.g. subscriptions plus advertising).
items.markingKey: Several sources of income spread risk, increase total revenue and use existing assets and customers more fully (e.g. subscriptions plus advertising). [1] for each relevant point identified and [1] for each point explained and applied to the case (2 × 2). Generic answers without application: maximum [2].

items.stem:
Read the extract.

In 2020 many airlines cut revenue expenditure such as staff costs through furlough schemes while delaying capital expenditure on new aircraft.

Explain why businesses need to distinguish between capital and revenue expenditure. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: Capital expenditure is recorded as assets and spread over their life through depreciation, while revenue expenditure is an expense in the period; mixing them distorts profit and asset values and leads to wrong finance choices.
items.markingKey: Capital expenditure is recorded as assets and spread over their life through depreciation, while revenue expenditure is an expense in the period; mixing them distorts profit and asset values and leads to wrong finance choices. [1] for each relevant point identified and [1] for each point explained and applied to the case (2 × 2). Generic answers without application: maximum [2].

items.stem: Explain the difference between loan capital and share capital.
items.answer: Share capital gives investors ownership and possible dividends but does not have to be repaid; loan capital must be repaid with interest but does not dilute ownership.
items.markingKey: Share capital gives investors ownership and possible dividends but does not have to be repaid; loan capital must be repaid with interest but does not dilute ownership. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between revenue expenditure and capital expenditure.
items.answer: Capital expenditure buys assets used for more than a year (machinery, buildings); revenue expenditure pays for day-to-day running costs used up within the year (wages, rent, materials).
items.markingKey: Capital expenditure buys assets used for more than a year (machinery, buildings); revenue expenditure pays for day-to-day running costs used up within the year (wages, rent, materials). items.stem: Last month Neon Gaming Ltd spent money on: an extension to the factory $18,000; monthly wages of shop staff $800; insurance premiums $1,500; a new delivery van $40,000; raw materials for this month's production $2,400. items.answer: Capital: an extension to the factory, a new delivery van = $58,000; revenue: monthly wages of shop staff, insurance premiums, raw materials for this month's production = $4,700.

items.stem: Café Andino pays monthly rent of €4,000 and management salaries of €3,000. Each unit costs €3.50 in materials and packaging, and sells for €10.50. In May it sold 2,500 units. Calculate the profit or loss, and classify rent and materials as fixed or variable costs.
items.answer: Profit = €26,250 − €15,750 = €10,500. Rent: fixed (does not change with output); materials: variable (change with output).
items.markingKey: TR 26,250 − TC 15,750 = 10,500. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for €10,500. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [1] classification.

items.stem: Using airlines during Covid-19 as an example, explain the difference between capital and revenue expenditure.
items.answer: In 2020 many airlines cut revenue expenditure such as staff costs through furlough schemes while delaying capital expenditure on new aircraft. Day-to-day running costs were reduced immediately while long-term asset purchases were postponed
items.markingKey: Context (In 2020 many airlines cut revenue expenditure such as staff costs through furlough schemes while delaying capital expenditure on new aircraft.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Day-to-day running costs were reduced immediately while long-term asset purchases were postponed – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the difference between capital and revenue expenditure.

items.stem: Baobab Juices needs equipment costing £120,000. Option A: a bank loan at 8% simple interest per year, repaid in full after 4 years. Option B: leasing the equipment for £3,790 a month for 4 years, after which it is returned. Calculate the total cost of each option and recommend one, giving one non-financial reason.
items.answer: A: £120,000 + interest £38,400 = £158,400 (and the firm owns the asset). B: £3,790 × 48 = £181,920 (no ownership). The loan is cheaper overall; non-financial: leasing includes maintenance/upgrades and preserves borrowing capacity, while the loan gives ownership and residual value.
items.markingKey: Interest = 120,000 × 8% × 4 = 38,400; loan total 158,400; lease total 3,790 × 48 = 181,920. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both totals. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [R1] justified recommendation.
